chunks: Hishām ibn Sālim asked Abā ʿAbdِ اللَّهِ عليه السلام:

About a roof upon which urine is passed, then the rain falls upon it so it drips and reaches the garment. He عليه السلام said: “There is no harm in it so long as what reaches it from the water is more than it.”

key_terms.السَّطْحِ: the roof or rooftop surface in question
key_terms.الْمَاءِ: the water whose amount is considered
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm or problem

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on rainwater dripping from a roof contaminated with urine onto clothing?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning water dripping from a roof that had been urinated upon when rain falls on it. Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام states that there is no harm if the amount of water is greater than the impurity, indicating a ruling related to ritual purity.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.4 - Hisham ibn Salim asked Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as)

about a man urinating on a roof, then rain falls on it causing water to drip onto clothes.
Imam (as) said: "There is no harm in it as long as the water that hits it is more than the urine”.
